Our exterior cleaning work in Melbourne

Our own photos, and only our own

Thirteen photographs of completed work. That is the entire library and we would rather show thirteen real ones than pad the page out with stock images of somebody else’s driveway, which is what the old website did.

  • Every image is a job we did
  • No stock photography
  • No staged before and after
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Our work

Why this page is honest rather than long

A gallery is the easiest thing on a cleaning website to fake, and most of them are. Stock libraries are full of pressure washers cutting a clean stripe through grime, and half the industry uses the same dozen images.

So this page is short. It is what we have actually photographed, captioned with what was done to it, and it will grow as the work does. If you want to see something closer to your own property, ask: tell us the surface and the suburb and we will send through the nearest job we have on file, whether or not it ever made it onto this page.

Hard surfaces

Driveways, paving and aggregate

The bulk of the work. Exposed aggregate is the standard Victorian driveway finish and it is also the most absorbent, which is why so much of this is staining rather than simple dirt.

The rust photograph is the stain before it was dealt with, not after. It is on the page because it is the most common thing people send us a picture of, and it is worth knowing what it looks like when it has been sitting long enough to go into the surface. Rust stain removal explains what can and cannot be pulled back out of it.

Glass and homes

Windows, pool areas and facades

Glass and the surfaces around it, which usually get done together because nobody wants clean windows above a green balustrade.

New builds and commercial

Handovers, and work that runs to a schedule

Post construction work is its own thing. The contamination is different, the deadline is a settlement date, and nobody gets a second go at it.

Reading a gallery

Three things worth knowing about any of them

A clean stripe proves very little

The classic half cleaned driveway shot is easy to produce and says nothing about whether the finished job was even. The useful question is what the whole surface looked like at the end, which is why these are finished shots rather than dramatic ones.

Before and after needs the same camera position

A genuine pair is shot from the same spot, in the same light, before and after. Anything else is two different photographs with a label on them, and we would rather publish none than publish those.

Ask for one like yours

Thirteen photographs will not include your exact surface. We can usually send through something much closer by email, because plenty of jobs get photographed without ever going on a website.

Questions

About the photographs

Why are there no before and after photos?

Because a genuine pair has to be shot from the same spot before and after, and we do not currently have a set that meets that bar. Rather than put up two loosely related photographs and label them, there are none here. The sliders on the home page are labelled as illustrations for that reason: they show the kind of change a clean makes, not a particular job.

It is a gap and it will get filled properly. In the meantime, a half cleaned surface mid job, like the alfresco shot above, shows the same difference honestly.

Can I see work done in my suburb?

Often, yes. Send the suburb and the surface and we will send back the nearest thing we have photographed. A lot of work never makes it onto a website.

Coverage by council and suburb shows where the work has been.

Do you photograph every job?

Not every one, and not always well. Finishing a driveway at five on a winter afternoon in the rain does not produce a photograph worth putting up.

If you want photos of your own job, ask at booking and you will get them whether or not they ever appear here.

Will you use photos of my property?

Only if you say yes. Nothing goes on the website, on social or into a quote for someone else without the owner agreeing to it, and a job can be photographed for your records only.

For body corporate and commercial work we ask the manager rather than assuming the contract covers it.
